paragraphs.text: Telegram bridge for DeepSeek Harness: text, voice, photos and project-per-topic sessions without ope
ning the desktop app
# dsh-tg-bridge

Drive DeepSeek Harness from Telegram. It runs on the
machine that already has the harness, and it an
swers in the chat where you asked.

A forum topic is a project: its own session, working directory, model,
permissions and language. Two
topics share the install and nothing else.

Never made a bot? QUICKSTART.md goes from "no account" to a bot
that answers, one step at a time.
## What it does

- **A model per topic.** `/model` lists the routes the profile declares — provider
and model togethe

r — and a tap switches this topic only. `/model <route> all`
moves the default the other topics foll

ow; `/model auto` hands the topic back.
A chat for thinking out loud and a chat for engineering no l

onger share one model.
- **A topic is a project.** `/cd my-app`, and every turn runs from that direc

tory —
on a permission-enabled profile the sandbox is narrowed to it too, so the agent
cannot write

outside the project.
- **One edited message per turn.** Steps, a timer and the cache hit rate, plus

the
reasoning in a collapsed block you can tap open. A long turn adds a second
collapsed block with

every tool call. `/stop` is a button on that message.
- **`/diff` — review the turn, one hunk at a t

ime.** The working tree is split into
files and hunks; every hunk gets two buttons: explain it, or r

evert just that
hunk. A button carries a hash of the hunk it was drawn from, so a press that
arrives

after the file moved on is refused instead of touching a line nobody was
looking at. `/diff stat` i

s the file list alone.
- **An endpoint from the chat.** `/endpoint add <id> <https://url/v1> <KEY_EN

V>
[model,model]` writes the provider without an AI turn, and the key itself is
never typed — only t

he name of the variable that holds it. The new models appear
on `/model` as routes.
- **Input: text,

voice, photos.** Any speech engine plugs in — a local script, any
command-line tool, or an OpenAI-c

ompatible API (see `docs/VOICE.md`)
— and the transcript is shown before the answer. A photo is read

by the turn's own
model through `read_image`, text and UI included; no second model is needed.
- **

Goal and checklist per topic.** `/goal`, `/tasks`; both survive restarts and
are prepended to every

turn.
- **Two scopes for every setting.** `/reasoning <mode> all` moves the default,
without `all` i

t moves this topic; language and pinning follow the same rule,
and `/crew use reviewer` gives one to

pic its own effort, permissions and agent
preset (four built-in sets, read-only, copyable).
[该节后续省略]
## First run

`setup.mjs` leaves a working bridge with these defaults, and none of them need
a decision before the

ves a working bridge with these defaults, and none of them need
a decision before the first message:
| Setting | Default | Where to change it |

| profile | `headless` | `/profile` |
| folder | the workspace you ran setup in | `/cd` |
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 24 (the version DeepSeek Harness ships; sessions are zstd-compressed)
- DeepSeek Harness

`0.2.1-rc.2` or newer in the `0.2.x` line (`>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`)
- DeepSeek Harness installed (`~/

.dsh/profiles/headless`)
- A Telegram bot token from @BotFather

The supported harness range is declared in `engines.dsh`; that field decides
compatibility on its ow

n (DSH ignores `peerDependencies` when it is present).
The range includes an explicit prerelease bra

nch, because a plain `<0.3.0`
silently excludes `0.2.2-*` builds. A future `0.3.0` needs an explicit

bump:
the bridge relies on the `0.2.x` CLI flags and profile layout.
### What it needs from DSH

The bridge is a client of the DSH CLI, and the surface it uses is small enough to
write down: `--pro

file`, `--json`, `--session-id`, `--expose-internals <cli.js>`
when the app binary runs the CLI, and

the `{"type": ...}` JSON events on stdout.
Profiles are read as files (`cordis.patch.yml`, `package

.json`) under
`~/.dsh/profiles`. `package.json` spells the supported range out in
`engines.dsh`, and

it is capped below `0.3.0` on purpose: a minor bump may rename
an event, and a bridge that guesses
is a bridge that answers with silence.
Two escape hatches, for a moved app or a DSH that ships differently:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`/doctor` prints the command a turn would actually run, so a machine where these
matter says so inst
ead of failing with an empty answer.

**As a DSH plugin** (the package carries a `dsh.bundle`; the catalog entry is
pending review):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin starts one bridge when DSH boots and stops it on shutdown; if a
bridge is already running

(for example from the scheduled task), it leaves it
alone. Run `npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest init ...`
first so a config exists.
What `init` does:
| What | Where |
| bot token | `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` → `refs.DSH_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`; other keys are left alone

|
| your id and working directory | `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/config.json`; an existing file is not overwrit

ten |
| `headless` profile | checked, with a hint on how to create it if missing |

`init` flags: `--cwd <path>` (default `~/Projects`), `--voice` (enable
voice transcription), `--dry-
run` (show what would be written, change nothing).
Optional provider settings live in `config.json`:
| Key | Meaning |
| `providerKeys` | extra env var names to pass to a turn, read from `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`; defa

ult `[]` |
| `pricesUrl` | retired: `/prices` always reads OpenRouter's public list and labels the n

umber as a reference for the model |
| `vision.patch` | opt-in overlay profile for photo turns; defa

ult `""` — the turn's own model reads images |
| `vision.enabled` | set `true` to run photo turns on

`vision.patch` instead of the topic profile |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The bridge is a single process with long polling. Each turn spawns a separate
CLI process that exits

after the answer, so "no DSH process" between
turns is normal, not a failure.
## Security

- `config.json`, `state.json`, `pending/`, logs are in `.gitignore` and never
end up in the reposito

ry.
- The token is stored in the DSH credentials store, not in code or config.
- The bridge only rep
lies to ids in `allowedUserIds`.
